canonical_definition:
Space of definitions. Across the surveyed work, the dominant framing is iterative revision of a model's own prior output after checking it against feedback. Most definitions describe identifying an error or deficiency and then producing a corrected or improved version, often over multiple rounds, with feedback coming from execution results, verifier messages, tool or environment errors, solver checks, critiques, or user feedback; some papers also frame it as reviewing a previous generation and answering again with that feedback. A smaller line of work casts it as a latent ability or capacity rather than just an observed task, but the common success criterion is still a revised answer, code artifact, plan, query, or action that is more correct, valid, or aligned than the initial one.

Variants. Variants span many artifacts and settings. The most common are code- and reasoning-centered forms, including self-debugging from execution feedback, proof and chain-of-thought correction, and iterative answer or response revision; papers also use names such as error correction, self-refinement, self-checking, and progressive or iterative refinement. Smaller variants target specific artifacts and domains, including SQL noise correction, query regeneration after execution failure, patch refinement, fact revision to add missing context, invalid SMILES correction, chart code revision, description revision against an image, tool-call retry after error messages, and action or plan correction after failed execution.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers measure it with 6 instruments. Linked instruments include FB-Bench, GSM8K, MOLERR2FIX, MR-Ben, and ToolAlpaca, plus 1 other instrument; the linked descriptions are mostly benchmarks or evaluation sets, and MOLERR2FIX is described as a four-stage Error-to-Fix evaluation pipeline, while MR-Ben is described as going beyond accuracy to assess locating reasoning errors, explaining them, and providing corrections. Across these measures, the recorded scoring language centers on handling feedback, revising outputs, and supplying corrections.

What it is taken as evidence of. Rather than tying it to one construct, papers link it to 16 constructs. The most frequent linked construct is Reasoning; other prominent links are Chain-of-thought reasoning, Coding ability, Generalization, and Instruction following ability, with 11 other constructs also linked. The relationship language is not uniform: most construct links are causal claims from self-correction to a construct, while Chain-of-thought reasoning is recorded as a related link rather than a causal one.

characterization_sections.label: Space of definitions.
characterization_sections.text: Across the surveyed work, the dominant framing is iterative revision of a model's own prior output after checking it against feedback. Most definitions describe identifying an error or deficiency and then producing a corrected or improved version, often over multiple rounds, with feedback coming from execution results, verifier messages, tool or environment errors, solver checks, critiques, or user feedback; some papers also frame it as reviewing a previous generation and answering again with that feedback. A smaller line of work casts it as a latent ability or capacity rather than just an observed task, but the common success criterion is still a revised answer, code artifact, plan, query, or action that is more correct, valid, or aligned than the initial one.

characterization_sections.label: Variants.
characterization_sections.text: Variants span many artifacts and settings. The most common are code- and reasoning-centered forms, including self-debugging from execution feedback, proof and chain-of-thought correction, and iterative answer or response revision; papers also use names such as error correction, self-refinement, self-checking, and progressive or iterative refinement. Smaller variants target specific artifacts and domains, including SQL noise correction, query regeneration after execution failure, patch refinement, fact revision to add missing context, invalid SMILES correction, chart code revision, description revision against an image, tool-call retry after error messages, and action or plan correction after failed execution.

characterization_sections.label: Space of elicitation and scores.
characterization_sections.text: Papers measure it with 6 instruments. Linked instruments include FB-Bench, GSM8K, MOLERR2FIX, MR-Ben, and ToolAlpaca, plus 1 other instrument; the linked descriptions are mostly benchmarks or evaluation sets, and MOLERR2FIX is described as a four-stage Error-to-Fix evaluation pipeline, while MR-Ben is described as going beyond accuracy to assess locating reasoning errors, explaining them, and providing corrections. Across these measures, the recorded scoring language centers on handling feedback, revising outputs, and supplying corrections.

characterization_sections.label: What it is taken as evidence of.
characterization_sections.text: Rather than tying it to one construct, papers link it to 16 constructs. The most frequent linked construct is Reasoning; other prominent links are Chain-of-thought reasoning, Coding ability, Generalization, and Instruction following ability, with 11 other constructs also linked. The relationship language is not uniform: most construct links are causal claims from self-correction to a construct, while Chain-of-thought reasoning is recorded as a related link rather than a causal one.
